source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Phil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Phil。

lines.en: And I'm Becca.
lines.zh: 我是 Becca。

lines.en: Sending emails is a big part of modern work, and most people try to write emails politely.
lines.zh: 寄電子郵件是現代工作很重要的一部分，大多數人都會盡量有禮貌地寫信。

lines.en: Most, but not all!
lines.zh: 大多數，但不是全部！

lines.en: Recently, BBC Radio 4 programme All in the Mind asked listeners to tell them what they find rude in emails.
lines.zh: 最近，BBC 第四電台的節目《All in the Mind》請聽眾分享他們覺得電子郵件裡哪些地方很沒禮貌。

lines.en: Here, presenter Claudia Hammond and guest Pete Olusoga discuss what listeners had to say: Rachel in Manchester says what annoys her is people who start their emails with just your name and without a simple greeting like 'hi'.
lines.zh: 主持人 Claudia Hammond 和來賓 Pete Olusoga 在這裡討論聽眾的說法：曼徹斯特的 Rachel 說，讓她不爽的是信件開頭只寫你的名字，連一句簡單的「嗨」都沒有。

lines.en: She says the unnecessary formality always has the effect of putting her immediately on the defensive.
lines.zh: 她說這種不必要的正式感，總是讓她立刻產生防衛心。

lines.en: We've got an anonymous one here, who recently received a single emoji in response to a carefully considered and worded email.
lines.zh: 這裡有一位匿名聽眾，最近寄出一封用心思考、仔細斟酌措辭的信，結果只收到一個表情符號當回覆。

lines.en: One listener doesn't like emails which start with just her name because they put her on the defensive.
lines.zh: 有位聽眾不喜歡只用她名字開頭的信，因為這會讓她產生防衛心。

lines.en: The phrase to put someone on the defensive means to do or say something which makes them feel threatened or unsure.
lines.zh: 「to put someone on the defensive」這個片語的意思是，做或說了某件事，讓對方覺得受到威脅或不確定。

lines.en: Another listener found it rude when their email was answered with a single emoji, and I think that would annoy me too.
lines.zh: 另一位聽眾覺得自己的信只收到一個表情符號回覆很沒禮貌，我想這也會讓我不爽。

lines.en: These emails are examples of people being uncivil – an adjective meaning rude or impolite.
lines.zh: 這些信都是有人 uncivil 的例子——這個形容詞的意思是粗魯或不禮貌。

lines.en: And just to note, the noun that goes with this is incivility.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，對應的名詞是 incivility。

lines.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing more about rude emails at work and, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會聽到更多關於職場無禮郵件的內容，一如往常也會學到一些實用的新詞彙，全都可以在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 找到。

lines.en: But first, I have a question for you, Phil.
lines.zh: 不過首先，Phil，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: Last year, thousands of US government workers received an email requiring them to justify their job by listing five things they had accomplished that week...
lines.zh: 去年，數千名美國政府員工收到一封電子郵件，要求他們列出當週完成的五件事，來證明自己的工作有存在的必要……

lines.en: or resign.
lines.zh: 否則就辭職。

lines.en: But who sent this email?
lines.zh: 那麼這封信是誰寄的？

lines.en: Was it: a) Donald Trump, b) JD Vance, or c) Elon Musk?
lines.zh: 是：a) 川普、b) JD 范斯，還是 c) 馬斯克？

lines.en: Ooh, I don't know...
lines.zh: 喔，我不知道……

lines.en: Maybe JD Vance?
lines.zh: 也許是 JD 范斯？

lines.en: We'll find out later in the programme.
lines.zh: 我們會在節目稍後揭曉。

lines.en: Now, according to some psychologists, rudeness in emails is based on a fight-or-flight response humans feel when stressed.
lines.zh: 根據一些心理學家的說法，電子郵件中的無禮，源自人在壓力下會產生的「戰或逃」反應。

lines.en: Here, psychologist Dr Emma Russell explains these responses for BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.
lines.zh: 這是心理學家 Emma Russell 博士在 BBC 第四電台《All in the Mind》中對這些反應的說明。

lines.en: So, a fight response is usually when we try to dominate or belittle other people.
lines.zh: 所謂「戰」的反應，通常是我們試圖壓制或貶低別人。

lines.en: Emails that are hostile in tone and language, or even cc'ing senior personnel in on the message in order to elevate an issue and put someone in their place.
lines.zh: 像是語氣和用字充滿敵意的信，甚至把資深人員加進副本，好把事情升級、讓對方知道自己的分量。

lines.en: Then the flight response is when people try to protect themselves by withdrawing or avoiding.
lines.zh: 而「逃」的反應，是人們藉由退縮或逃避來保護自己。

lines.en: They won't reply, or if they do reply, maybe they don't answer all of the points in the email.
lines.zh: 他們不回信，或就算回了，也可能沒有回答信裡所有的問題。

lines.en: They're just trying to get it off their plate.
lines.zh: 他們只是想把這件事從自己手上丟掉。

lines.en: The fight response can make us belittle someone – make them feel inferior or unimportant.
lines.zh: 「戰」的反應可能讓我們貶低別人——讓對方覺得自己低人一等或不重要。

lines.en: For example, a boss sends a group email in which they give someone else the credit for the work you did.
lines.zh: 例如，主管寄了一封群組信，把你做的工作功勞歸給別人。

lines.en: The boss wants to put you in your place – an idiom meaning to show someone that they are less important than they think they are.
lines.zh: 主管想 put you in your place——這個慣用語的意思是讓某人知道，他們沒有自己以為的那麼重要。

lines.en: The flight response, meanwhile, can be seen when co-workers ignore your message or give a quick, unhelpful reply.
lines.zh: 另一方面，「逃」的反應可以從同事不理你的訊息，或只給一個快速、沒幫助的回覆看出來。

lines.en: Such colleagues want to get work off their plate – another idiom, meaning to remove tasks from your own workload and give them to someone else to deal with.
lines.zh: 這樣的同事想 get work off their plate——這是另一個慣用語，意思是把工作從自己的工作量中移走，丟給別人處理。

lines.en: Unfortunately, when stressed and working to a deadline it's hard to make sure all your emails are polite.
lines.zh: 可惜的是，在壓力下趕截止期限時，很難確保每封信都有禮貌。

lines.en: That's what Emma Russell said when she spoke to BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.
lines.zh: 這是 Emma Russell 在 BBC 第四電台《All in the Mind》中說的。

lines.en: Because we're operating in these environments where we are all quite frazzled, we are more at risk of engaging in incivility.
lines.zh: 因為我們都在讓人疲憊不堪的環境中工作，所以更容易做出無禮的行為。

lines.en: We're more likely to be uncivil when we're frazzled – an informal adjective describing feeling tired or anxious because you're doing too many things at the same time.
lines.zh: 我們 frazzled 時更容易無禮——這個非正式的形容詞，形容因為同時做太多事而感到疲憊或焦慮。

lines.en: Luckily, there are ways to help.
lines.zh: 幸好，有一些方法可以幫忙。

lines.en: If you feel angry when writing an email, pause before you hit send.
lines.zh: 如果你寫信時感到生氣，按下寄出前先停一下。

lines.en: One day it might save your friendship or even your job! OK.
lines.zh: 有一天這可能會救了你的友誼，甚至你的工作！好。

lines.en: Becca, I'm going to politely ask you to please reveal the answer to your question.
lines.zh: Becca，我要很有禮貌地請你揭曉問題的答案。

lines.en: Of course, Phil.
lines.zh: 當然，Phil。

lines.en: I asked you who sent the email requiring workers to justify their employment or resign.
lines.zh: 我問你，是誰寄了那封要求員工證明自己工作有必要、否則就辭職的信。

lines.en: I said that I thought it might have been JD Vance.
lines.zh: 我說我覺得可能是 JD 范斯。

lines.en: Well, we're not going to fire you, Phil, but you are wrong.
lines.zh: 嗯，我們不會開除你，Phil，但你答錯了。

lines.en: The correct answer was Elon Musk.
lines.zh: 正確答案是馬斯克。

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with the idiom 'put someone on the defensive', meaning to make someone feel threatened or unsure.
lines.zh: 好。我們來複習學到的詞彙，首先是慣用語「put someone on the defensive」，意思是讓某人覺得受到威脅或不確定。

lines.en: The adjective 'uncivil' means impolite, and we have a similar noun that's 'incivility'.
lines.zh: 形容詞「uncivil」的意思是不禮貌，類似的名詞是「incivility」。

lines.en: 'To belittle someone' means to make them feel inferior or unimportant.
lines.zh: 「To belittle someone」的意思是讓某人覺得自己低人一等或不重要。

lines.en: If you put someone in their place, you show them that they're not as important as they think they are.
lines.zh: 如果你 put someone in their place，就是讓對方知道他們沒有自己以為的那麼重要。

lines.en: 'To get something off your plate' means to give someone else a task or problem instead of dealing with it yourself.
lines.zh: 「To get something off your plate」的意思是把工作或問題交給別人，而不是自己處理。

lines.en: And finally, if you're frazzled, you feel tired or anxious because you're doing too much.
lines.zh: 最後，如果你 frazzled，就是因為做太多事而感到疲憊或焦慮。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了。

lines.en: If you want to know more about communication at work, check out our series Office English.
lines.zh: 如果你想多了解職場溝通，可以看看我們的系列節目《Office English》。

lines.en: It's on our website, along with a quiz and a worksheet for this episode, and that's bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 它在我們的網站上，還有這一集的測驗和學習單，網址是 bbclearningenglish.com。

lines.en: But now it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Bye!
lines.zh: 拜拜！
